Stored on the<br>chunks, a file cut into twenty pieces carried twenty copies of<br>its history — which is what made a real history unaffordable.<br><br>One point per file also gives a deterministic id, so the API<br>answers "who imports this?" with a retrieve by key rather than<br>a scan of 32 630 points.<br><br>A change of embedding_model or chunking_version recreates<br>kalisio_code and kalisio_code_files together: chunks written<br>under an older contract cannot even be matched for deletion." style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=2;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="820" y="540" width="740" height="230" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n12" value="Change detection reads the digests from two places: the chunk payloads (the file has chunks) and the file<br>entries (the file yields none). relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n30" value="The one thing to remember about the mount<br><br>Starlette matches a mount only below itself, so /mcp used to be answered with a 307 onto /mcp/. Behind the<br>ingress that Location carried the scheme uvicorn sees — http — nginx bounced it back to /mcp without the slash,<br>and every client looped until it gave up on TooManyRedirects. Both spellings are now served directly, and<br>api/bin.py passes proxy_headers=True with forwarded_allow_ips="*" so the proxy's headers are trusted." vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="690" width="760" height="210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n7" value="<b>The rest of the /mcp surface</b><br>GET /mcp/ → opens an SSE stream (stateless: carries nothing)<br>PUT /mcp/ → 405, as JSON-RPC<br><br>JSON-RPC methods answered:<br> initialize the handshake, negotiates the version<br> tools/list the two tools and their schemas<br> tools/call runs one<br> ping keep-alive<br> resources/list answers, empty — none are exposed<br> prompts/list answers, empty" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontFamily=Courier New;fontSize=10;spacing=6;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#cccccc;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="840" y="690" width="740" height="210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n8" value="Reading the two zeroes of get_file_context<br><br>indexed: true · dependent_count: 0 → the graph covers this file and nothing imports it. A refactor is safe.<br>indexed: false · dependent_count: 0 → the graph cannot speak for this file. Nothing can be concluded.<br><br>Three cases produce the second: no entry at all, an entry written by an ingestion older than the graph, and a<br>file type the graph does not cover (markdown, json). They collapse on purpose — the honest answer is the same.<br>Between deploying the graph and the first nightly run that builds it, every file in the corpus is in that state." style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=2;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="930" width="1540" height="180" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> <diagram id="built-graph" name="built · dependency graph"> <mxGraphModel dx="1400" dy="800" grid="1" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="1" page="1" pageScale="1" pageWidth="1600" pageHeight="1000" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="n1" value="ingestion/pipeline/dependency_graph.py — step 7.
